newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Initial NZ$90 mln planned in Pacific Retail CP-BNZ.
newsitem.headline: Initial NZ$90 mln planned in Pacific Retail CP-BNZ.

text.p: Bank of New Zealand said on Tuesday it would issue an initial NZ$90 million of commercial paper in its securitisation programme for Pacific Retail Group Ltd.

Philippe Blin, senior manager of BNZ's Structured Finance Group, said approximately NZ$30 million of paper would be offered to the market in each of three initial tenders on January 24, February 20 and March 20. "We'll be tapping the market over a period of time," he said.

Under the scheme, Pacific Retail's hire purchase portfolio is assigned to a 100 percent subsidiary, Pacific Retail Finance, and the debt is then sold to a securitisation vehicle called Pacific Retail Securities Ltd.

The latter will fund itself through the wholesale debt market in New Zealand via short-term 30, 60 and 90-day notes which will be indexed on the bank bill rate and offered to institutional investors by tender.

Demand for the paper will determine the margin over the bank bill rate. "It is expected that the margin will be very fine because the credit rating of this paper is the highest credit rating you can get, it's A-1+," Blin said.

Currently, approximately NZ$100 million of debt is to be covered by approximately $90 million of notes. Blin said the balance would be funded by subordinated debt, the whole of which will be placed with Pacific Retail Ltd.

The total size of the CP programme is set at NZ$250 million, to accommodate expected growth of the business over the next few years. Pacific Retail, formerly Noel Leeming, is New Zealand's biggest retailer of home appliances and consumer electronics.
